model: Bank FCFE at cost of equity (J-GAAP profit attributable less book-growth retention, net debt zero, per ADS; engine route)

historical_growth.revenue_basis: IFRS total operating income (CSV Revenue) FY2023 3,790,676 / FY2021 3,165,585 -> FY2026 4,841,783 JPY m. Gross interest income (kpis BankInterestIncome 1.75tn -> 6.93tn) is rate-inflated and not used.
historical_growth.eps_basis: IFRS diluted EPS JPY 222.63 (FY2023) / 167.16 (FY2021) -> 295.99 (FY2026), all restated for the Oct-2024 3-for-1 split, pre-2026-split. FY2025 (122.36) was a mark-to-market trough.
historical_growth.equity_basis: IFRS equity attributable to SMFG shareholders 12,664,991 (FY2023) / 11,559,235 (FY2021) -> 15,856,895 (FY2026), after ~JPR 850bn of buybacks over FY2023-26 and FVOCI swings.
historical_growth.fcf_note: Not meaningful for a bank: OCF swings with deposit and trading flows (FY2023 -5.24tn, FY2025 +3.07tn, FY2026 -6.46tn).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 6.5% vs EPS 5yr 12.1% and 3yr 10.0%: >30% divergence. Earnings outgrew book because BOJ normalisation lifted ROE (margin, not balance-sheet growth) and buybacks shrank the share count 6.5% over five years. The forward path therefore separates the rate step (Y1-Y3) from balance-sheet growth (2-3.5%/yr) rather than extrapolating either CAGR.
historical_growth.notes: SBC-zero market: SBC-adjusted and reported series coincide. CAGRs are on IFRS; the valuation stream is J-GAAP (see inputs.earnings_basis_note).

scenario_narratives.base: SMFG earns the JPY 1.7tn FY2027 guide as the BOJ's move to 1.00% feeds through its JPY ~190tn deposit base, reaches ~JPY 1.9tn by Mar-2029 as credit costs normalise and disposal gains fade, then compounds at 1.5-3.5% balance-sheet growth. Incremental ROE ~12% against an 8.5% JPY cost of equity supports a fair value of ~1.43x book, below the ~1.6x the market pays after an ~80% re-rating in twelve months.
scenario_narratives.bull: Management delivers the medium-term plan on time -- JPY 2tn profit and 13% ROTE by Mar-2029 -- with the BOJ at 1.25-1.5%, sticky deposit pricing, a strong wealth/capital-markets cycle from governance reform, and a disciplined Asia build (YES Bank) after exiting Jenius. ROE 14% justifies ~1.6x book.
scenario_narratives.bear: The rate step is already in the run-rate; the BOJ pauses, overseas credit costs rise, and cross-shareholding gains thin. Profit slips to JPY 1.55tn and grows 1-2%. A 10% ROE bank in a shrinking market is worth ~1.2x book, roughly a quarter below the current price.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A bank is valued on the equity cash flow it can distribute while funding its own balance-sheet growth, discounted at the cost of equity in the currency of the flows (JPY), with no net-debt bridge because deposits and wholesale funding are operating liabilities. SMFG's earnings have been re-based by BOJ normalisation; the question is how much of that is run-rate versus still-to-come, and whether a ~12% incremental ROE deserves ~1.6x book. The market's current multiple needs roughly the bull case (13-14% ROTE, plan delivered) to be fair value.
key_risks_to_valuation: BOJ pauses or reverses: the Y1-Y3 earnings step is the largest value driver and depends on policy continuing toward ~1.25%.
Overseas/global-corporate credit costs normalise faster than NIM expands (US tariffs, geopolitics); the bear case carries this, the base only partly.
J-GAAP profit includes realised cross-shareholding gains (~JPY 0.3-0.4tn/yr) that are finite; if they fade faster the base path is too high by low single digits.
Earnings-basis gap: IFRS attributable profit is 28% below J-GAAP; a reader who anchors on the 20-F EPS will see ~22x, not ~16x.
ADS bridge: the valuation is per ADS = 1.2 post-split / 0.6 pre-split shares at 157.83 JPY/USD; a 10% yen move is a ~10% USD move in IV with no change in the JPY business.
Guidance and buyback-progress anchors are from the Analysis JSON (web), not an extracted filing; the Nov-2026 1H results should be checked against them.
Securities portfolio mark-to-market (JGBs as rates rise) and Basel III finalisation could absorb the CET1 surplus assumed distributable.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API (NYSE ADS) at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 15.18-27.62. FX Yahoo JPY=X at the time in fx_note. Parity against Tokyo 8316.T (post-split) in fx_note.
data_sources.financials: SMFG 20-F FY2026 (IFRS, year to 31-Mar-2026): J-GAAP reconciliation (Item 5), cover share count, Note 25 (2026 Stock Split, buybacks), Note 42 (dividends), goodwill note; SMFG_Metrics.csv / core_metrics (IFRS, JPY millions, FY2017-FY2026); kpis (DividendsPaid, ShareRepurchases, ProfitBeforeTax).
data_sources.qualitative: SMFG_Analysis.json (2026-10-04): medium-term plan targets, FY2027 JPY 1.7tn guide, DPS JPY 157, CET1 12.41%, YES Bank stake, Jenius wind-down, buyback progress to 30-Jun-2026.

inputs.base_revenue_note: NOT bank revenue. The engine stream is FY0 (year to 31-Mar-2026) Japanese-GAAP profit attributable to owners of parent, JPY 1,583bn (20-F FY2026 Item 5 'Reconciliation with Japanese GAAP': J-GAAP net profit JPY 1,584,815m vs IFRS net profit 1,194,960m total / 1,137,557m attributable; SMFG_20F_FY2026.txt:22824-22845). Margin 100%, tax 0%, SBC/D&A 0% because the stream is already after tax, provisions, NCI and funding cost; the 'capex' path is the equity retained to grow the balance sheet (retention = balance-sheet growth / incremental ROE).
inputs.earnings_basis_note: J-GAAP rather than the 20-F IFRS figure because dividends (40% payout target; FY2026 DPS JPY 157 = 38% of J-GAAP), buybacks, the 10% ROE / 13% ROTE targets, FSA capital and the FY2027 JPY 1.7tn guide are all set on J-GAAP, and the Tokyo market prices SMFG on it (~16x trailing J-GAAP vs ~22x IFRS at the price_as_of close). The JPY 447bn IFRS/J-GAAP gap is mostly realised gains on cross-shareholding sales (recon item 3 'Investment securities' +418bn: J-GAAP recycles them through P&L, IFRS FVOCI election sends them straight to equity) and hedge/derivative timing (+286bn), net of tax (-271bn). Those disposal gains are real cash but finite (cross-shareholding reduction programme), which is one reason the base growth path decays below management's 'toward JPY 2tn by FY2028' aspiration rather than extrapolating it.
inputs.share_count_basis: ADS-EQUIVALENTS, not ordinary shares, on the PRE-2026-split basis the CSV uses. Ordinary shares outstanding at 31-Mar-2026: 3,827,498,140 issued less 10,632,119 treasury = 3,816.87m (20-F FY2026 cover, SMFG_20F_FY2026.txt:19378-19381); dilutive stock options 0.77m (EPS note :29186) ignored. Less ~27.5m repurchased under the JPY 180bn / 40m-share programme 14-May to 31-Jul-2026 (17.6m for JPY 108.5bn by 30-Jun-2026 per the Analysis JSON; assumed completed in full at ~JPY 6,500/sh; cancelled 20-Aug-2026) = ~3,789.4m pre-split shares. 1 ADS = 0.6 pre-split share (20-F cover: 'each ADS representing 3/5 of one share'), so 3,789.4 / 0.6 = 6,315.7m ADS-equivalents. The 2026 Stock Split (2-for-1, record 30-Sep-2026, effective 1-Oct-2026; 20-F :28678-28680, Yahoo 8316.T split event 2:1) doubles the ordinary count to ~7,579m and the ADS ratio to 1 ADS = 1.2 new shares; it does not change the number of ADS-equivalents, so all per-ADS values here are unaffected. Held flat: buybacks are the distribution of the FCFE being valued, not extra value.
inputs.net_debt_note: Deposits (JPY ~190tn), borrowings (10.6tn) and debt securities in issue (16.6tn) are operating funding for a bank, not net debt; the stream is post-interest, so nothing is deducted. CSV total_debt / cash columns are balance-sheet lines, not a bridge.
inputs.fcf_note: FY0 FCFE = J-GAAP profit 1,583,000 x (1 - 25% retention at 3% balance-sheet growth / 12% ROE) = 1,187,250. Actual FY2026 distributions were JPY 540bn dividends + 250bn buybacks = 790bn (50% payout); the difference is CET1 accumulation (12.41% at 31-Mar-2026 vs ~10% internal target) and growth investment (YES Bank 20% stake). Reported OCF (-6.46tn FY2026) is deposit/trading flow and is not FCF for a bank.
inputs.sbc_source: SBC-zero market: restricted-share / BIP-trust executive compensation and the Mar-2024 employee share plan are immaterial against JPY 1.6tn profit and are inside operating expense in the stream (20-F FY2026 Note on share-based compensation, :25-40). House and street bases coincide.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2026 (to Mar-2026) ShareRepurchases JPY 250.4bn (kpis; IFRS cash flow), FY2025 251.4bn, FY2024 211.2bn. Dividends paid FY2026 JPY 540.1bn (JPY 140/sh recognised in the year; JPY 157/sh declared for FY2026 = 78 interim + 79 final, Note 42 :29381-29404).
inputs.ads_ratio_note: Ordinary shares per ADS, PRE-2026-split basis (matches core_metrics/CSV shares_outstanding, which is pre-split): 1 ADS = 0.6 pre-split ordinary share (20-F FY2026 cover, 'each ADS representing 3/5 of one share'). Used by sanity_check.py to convert core_metrics per-ordinary-share book/earnings to per-ADS before dividing into the USD ADS price -- without it, historical P/B and P/E print understated by the ratio (same false-pass class as HSBC/LYG/MFG/MUFG). The 2026 2-for-1 split (effective 1-Oct-2026) doubles the live ratio to 1 ADS = 1.2 new shares, but does not change this value since the CSV's shares_outstanding column stays on the pre-split basis until a future extraction restates it.
inputs.fx_note: fx_rate converts JPY (model) to USD (quote): 1/157.83 = 0.0063359 USD per JPY, Yahoo Finance JPY=X at 2026-10-04T04:21Z. Per-share values are per ADS-equivalent, so intrinsic_value is USD per SMFG ADS, comparable to current_price; the *_jpy twins are JPY per ADS. JPY per post-split ordinary share (8316.T basis from 1-Oct-2026) = *_jpy / 1.2; per pre-split share = *_jpy / 0.6. Parity check: Tokyo 8316.T close JPY 3,321 (2026-10-02 06:30Z, post-split) x 1.2 / 157.83 = USD 25.25 vs the NYSE ADS close at price_as_of, +0.6% -- confirming the rate direction AND the post-split ratio of 1.2 new shares per ADS (the 0.6 ratio printed on the June-2026 20-F cover would put the ADS at USD 12.63, half where it trades; the ADS monthly series shows no halving across 1-Oct-2026, so the depositary doubled the ratio exactly as it did 0.2 -> 0.6 at the Oct-2024 3-for-1 split). The Analysis JSON's '1 ADS = 0.6 share' is the pre-split figure.
inputs.units_note: Money in JPY millions (matching core_metrics); shares in millions of ADS-equivalents; per-share values in JPY per ADS, converted to USD at fx_rate.
inputs.fy0_note: FY2026 = year ended 31-Mar-2026 (CSV/20-F labelling). In SMFG's own convention this is 'FY2025'; management's 'FY2026 JPY 1.7tn' guide is the year to 31-Mar-2027 = this model's Y1, and 'toward JPY 2tn / 13% ROTE by FY2028' is the year to 31-Mar-2029 = Y3. The Analysis JSON's '2026-Q2 (six months to Sept 2026)' entry is the half to 30-Sep-2025 (J-GAAP 1H profit JPY 933.5bn); 1H to Sep-2026 is not yet reported.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-02T20:00:03Z NYSE regular close (Friday); Yahoo chart API
inputs.share_count_date: 2026-07-31 (31-Mar-2026 register less the May-Jul 2026 buyback, estimated)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Single JPY cost of equity of 8.5% across all three scenarios (risk charged once, through the scenario weights). Built in the flows' own currency: 10y JGB ~2.0% (BOJ policy rate 1.00% since Jun-2026) + beta ~1.15 x Japan ERP ~5.5% = ~8.3%, rounded up for G-SIB leverage and rate-path sensitivity; same as the MUFG build (8.5%) and below MFG (9.0%) because SMFG's ROE and capital are closer to MUFG's. Not a WACC: the stream is post-interest, so it is discounted at the cost of equity and no debt is deducted. A USD rate would overcharge the JPY flows by the rate differential.
inputs.lease_treatment: N/A -- lease costs are inside bank operating expense and therefore inside the post-tax profit stream.
inputs.nci_treatment: Stream is J-GAAP profit attributable to owners of parent (after NCI and after distributions to other equity instrument holders, which J-GAAP treats as liabilities -- recon item 11); IFRS NCI is JPY 179bn of equity. No further bridge deduction; charged once.
inputs.notes: MODEL: Bank -> residual-income / FCFE family per dcf-methods routing (deposits are not debt, OCF is meaningless), implemented as FCFE at cost of equity through the component engine with net_debt = 0, exactly as the house megabank precedents MUFG, MFG, HSBC, LYG (2026-10-04). FCFE = J-GAAP profit x (1 - retention), retention = balance-sheet/RWA growth / incremental ROE (12% base, 14% bull, 10% bear); terminal retention = g / ROE so the Gordon value is internally consistent. First valuation of SMFG (no memory entry, no prior DCF). BOOK CHECK: IFRS equity attributable JPY 15,857bn (J-GAAP 15,933bn); goodwill 325bn + other intangibles ~917bn -> tangible book ~14,615bn = ~JPY 3,829 per pre-split share; at the price_as_of close SMFG trades ~1.6x book, ~1.73x TBV, ~16x trailing and ~14.8x guided J-GAAP earnings. The weighted IV implies ~1.40x book / ~13.1x guided earnings (base ~1.43x, bull ~1.60x, bear ~1.16x). DATA CAVEATS: the FY2027 JPY 1.7tn guide, the YES Bank stake and the buyback progress to 30-Jun-2026 come from the Analysis JSON (web sources), not an extracted filing line -- only 20-Fs are in Extracted/; the Nov-2026 1H results and any guidance revision should trigger an update. The CSV's shares_outstanding column (3,843.2) is the diluted weighted average, pre-2026-split.

bear.growth_rates_note: Y1 JPY 1.55tn: BOJ pauses at 1.00%, overseas/global-corporate credit costs rise with tariff and geopolitical stress (flagged by management as the watch item), cross-shareholding gains thin, Jenius wind-down costs; then low-single-digit growth capped by Japanese demographics and a weaker yen's translation drag on domestic ROE.
bear.capex_pct_path_note: Retention = balance-sheet growth (2.5, 2.5, 2, 2, 2, 1.5, 1.5, 1, 1, 1%) / incremental ROE 10% (ROE stalls at the level just reached; Basel III finalisation absorbs capital). Terminal 10% = 1.0% / 10%.
bear.narrative: Normalisation stalls: the rate tailwind is already in the run-rate, credit costs normalise against overseas exposure, and SMFG is a 10%-ROE bank in a shrinking market -- still worth more than book, but not the ~1.6x the market pays.

base.growth_rates_note: Y1 (to Mar-2027) = JPY 1.70tn guide (+7.4%); Y2 +6% on the full-year effect of BOJ at 1.00-1.25% and NIM toward ~1.0%, net of rising overseas credit costs; Y3 +5% to ~JPY 1.89tn, a little short of the 'toward JPY 2tn by FY2028' aspiration as cross-shareholding disposal gains fade; then balance-sheet growth decaying to 1.5% in a shrinking home market.
base.ebitda_margin_path_note: Stream is already post-tax distributable earnings.
base.capex_pct_path_note: Retention = balance-sheet/RWA growth (3.5, 3.5, 3, 3, 2.5, 2.5, 2, 2, 2, 1.5%) / incremental J-GAAP ROE 12% (FY2026 actual ~10.5% on average book, ROTE ~12%; management targets 13% ROTE by FY2028). Terminal 12.5% = g 1.5% / ROE 12%. Implied payout 71-88% vs FY2026 actual 50% (dividends 540bn + buybacks 250bn on 1,583bn) -- the excess is capital SMFG is currently accumulating above its 10% CET1 target and deploying into Asia (YES Bank).
base.narrative: BOJ normalisation is banked at 1.00% and earnings step up to the JPY 1.7tn guide, approach JPY 1.9tn by Y3, then grow with a slow Japanese balance sheet plus Asia; incremental ROE holds ~12%, above an 8.5% cost of equity.

bull.growth_rates_note: Y1 JPY 1.75tn (guide beaten as in FY2026, when guidance was raised twice); Y3 ~JPY 2.0tn -- the medium-term plan hit on time with ROTE 13%; BOJ to 1.25-1.5% with low deposit betas, benign credit, and a sustained capital-markets/wealth cycle from Japanese governance reform.
bull.capex_pct_path_note: Retention = balance-sheet growth (4, 4, 3.5, 3.5, 3, 3, 2.5, 2.5, 2.5, 2%) / incremental ROE 14% (the 13-15% ROTE aspiration delivered). Terminal 14.3% = 2.0% / 14%.
bull.narrative: The plan is delivered: JPY 2tn profit and 13% ROTE by Mar-2029, further BOJ hikes with sticky deposit pricing, credit costs stay low, and SMFG re-rates toward global-bank multiples.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 16x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear at 25%, above the 15% house default, because the earnings step rests on one policy variable (the BOJ rate path, which the Analysis rates the dominant driver and risk) and on credit costs that are cyclically low against rising overseas exposure. Base at 50%: FY2026 beat guidance and the FY2027 guide follows the same mechanics. Bull at 25%, below the 35% default, because it needs several independent things at once (further hikes, low deposit betas, benign credit, a capital-markets cycle, Asia execution) and the market has already re-rated the stock ~80% in a year. Matches the house megabank precedent (MUFG, MFG, HSBC at 25/50/25).
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
